neighbours.label: Anticipated source or means: fires on the noun or copula at the point where a statement of origin is expected next (take their water → from; achieve their results → by; where did X → come from; their power is → generated by). Plain descriptions with no origin frame stay quiet
fire: Most farms on the plateau draw their irrigation water from deep wells.
Nearly all of the island's electricity is produced by burning imported diesel.
Scientists still argue about where the Moon's water came from originally.
These antibiotics achieve their results by blocking the bacterial cell wall.
The monastery gets its income from selling cheese and honey.
Children often ask where babies come from when a sibling is born.
The town takes its name from a chapel that once stood on the hill.
Solar panels get their energy from sunlight rather than from fuel.
quiet: Most farms on the plateau are small and grow wheat or barley.
Nearly all of the island's beaches are rocky and windy in winter.
Scientists still enjoy visiting the observatory on clear nights.
These antibiotics are expensive and must be kept in a refrigerator.
The monastery closes its gates at sunset every evening.
Children often fall asleep quickly after a long day outside.
The town has a market square with a fountain in the middle.
Solar panels look dark blue and feel smooth to the touch.
